'''[[Urcea]]''' has a universal multi-payer health care system paid for by a combination of statutory, state-funded health insurance officially called [[Ministry_of_Administration_of_the_Realm_(Urcea)#Agency_for_the_King.27s_Health_Aid_Administration|King's Health Aid]] (KHA) and private health-insurance. The system, which provides a public health insurance option, sees approximately 65% of citizens using the KHA System and the remaining percent using private health insurance plans. In the 2014-15 fiscal year, expenditures on the King's Health Aid was approximately $4.3 trillion dollars, or around 6% of the GDP and around $3,024 per capita.

In 2020, Urcea ranked highly in the world in life expectancy (80.5 years for men). It had a very low infant mortality rate (4.1 per 1,000 live births), and it ranked highly in the number of practicing physicians, at 3.7 per 1,000 persons. '''Sejdzas sandbox''' is a term used in political science to describe a characteristic mode of policymaking historically associated with [[Nasastan]] and its predecessor states. The concept describes the deliberate alteration and experimental implementation of existing political, economic, social, or institutional systems while retaining an identifiable means of reversing the intervention if it produces an unacceptable outcome. It is generally divided into two principal phases, Sejdzaisation and sandboxing, preceded by an analytical process commonly termed pre-Sejdzaisation. Although the term Sejdzas sandbox was coined only in the early 21st century, the practice it describes predates the modern Nasastani state by many centuries. Recorded examples have been identified as far back as the reign of [[Kooroush Qajar]] (1056-1091), while similar institutional arrangements were subsequently employed by the [[Qajar dynasty]], the [[Grand Duchy of Nasastan]], the [[Lunarian Empire]], and the [[Nasastan|National Federation of Nasastan]]. articles.summary: , in 2010.]] Urcea is divided into thirty-four constituent entities (known variously as provinces, crownlands, or states) which are further subdivided into dioceses and then municipalities. Local government throughout Urcea retains the same form throughout the provinces, though in some instances the…
articles.wikitextSnippet:
[[File:FEMA - 32463 - SBA at Findlay Town Meeting in Ohio.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A meeting of the communal assembly in Icron, [[Ardthirium]], in [[2010]].]]
[[Urcea]] is divided into thirty-four constituent entities (known variously as [[Province (Urcea)|provinces]], [[Crownland (Urcea)|crownlands]], or [[State (Urcea)|states]]) which are further subdivided into dioceses and then municipalities. Local government throughout Urcea retains the same form throughout the provinces, though in some instances the nomenclature and titles of officeholders and public institutions may vary. Every part of Urcea is incorporated within a municipal government, precluding the use of {{wp|unincorporated area}}s. 

Municipalities play an important role in the function of public administration in Urcea, and they typically take on three distinct forms of government. They are the primary instruments through which basic public services are provided to Urceans, including running water, local road maintenance, and the provision of public education. Diocesan governments - the second lowest level of government - are responsible for the administration of justice and also serve critical functions within Urcea's electoral and political systems.  Beyond their governmental role, municipalities in Urcea tend to have strong cultural associations and identity attached to them.

Each of the 34 [[Urcea]]n provinces, states, and crownlands holds {{wp|primary election}}s help nominate individual candidates for the office of [[Procurator]]. This process is designed to choose the candidates that will represent their political parties in the [[Elections in Urcea|general election]]. The primary process generally developed over time. It was established [[History_of_Urcea_(1902-1943)#Mid-war_political_changes|among political changes]] in the [[Second Great War]], though a rudimentary primary system was in place between [[1903]] and [[1944]]. 

Individuals who seek the office of Procurator do not receive the official endorsement of [[Political parties in Urcea|party apparatuses]]. Instead, they must gather ballot access petitions equal to 5% of the enrolled voters of a party within an individual province, crownland, or state in order to qualify for that subdivison's procuratorial primary. The ballot access requirements must be met forty days prior to the primary being held, and oftentimes lesser known candidates will only initially gather ballot access signatures in some of the earliest provinces so as to gain enough momentum to employ petition circulators in the later provinces.

articles.wikitextSnippet:
'''Mass surveillance in Nasastan''' refers to the large-scale collection, retention, processing and administrative use of information concerning the population of [[Nasastan]] by state institutions and associated organizations. Although surveillance practices existed in rudimentary forms before the establishment of the modern system, mass surveillance is generally considered to have begun ''de facto'' in 1951 and to have become institutionalized during the late 1950s and 1960s. The contemporary Nasastani system differs substantially from conventional secret-police models. Whereas surveillance during the early 1950s was principally directed against political opponents and groups regarded as threats to the state, the post-1950s system increasingly treated information as an administrative resource. Surveillance became associated with public administration, judicial proceedings, healthcare regulation, security, demographic policy and, eventually, digital services and artificial intelligence.

A central feature of the Nasastani model is the absence of a conventional legal right to privacy from the state. This principle developed partly from the historical distinction between ''Saméné'', referring primarily to interpersonal privacy, and ''Préwatność'', a later legal concept concerning privacy from the state and society at large. {{Politics of Nasastan}}

The [[Nasastan|National Federation of Nasastan]] is a federal parliamentary authoritarian republic characterized by a political system of [[Guided democracy|managed pluralism]]. Under the [[Constitution of Nasastan|Constitution of 1937]], political participation is structured through a unique asymmetric bicameral legislature that separates economic governance from sociocultural deliberation. While the country permits a degree of multiparty competition, the [[Ethnofederalist Social Nasastani National Party]] (SNNSP) functions as the dominant legal and administrative framework of the state. Political activity in Nasastan is divided according to the specific competencies of the two parliamentary chambers; The [[Purokal]] (Economic Chamber)''':''' Membership is strictly restricted to representatives of the SNNSP. Economic debate is not conducted between rival parties but within five internal ideological factions of the SNNSP, which range from far-left to far-right economic currents. The [[Rada]] (Sociocultural Chamber) operates under a system of full party plurality, serving as the primary forum for multiparty competition and ideological contestation. Despite the plurality found in the Rada, all sociocultural legislation is subject to the absolute veto of the [[Načelnik]], the cultural sentinel of the state. The '''League of Nations Service Medal''' ('''LoNM''') is an {{wp|international military decoration}} established by the [[League of Nations]] on September 14, 2025. The decoration is the first international award ever created by the League of Nations and recognized the multi-national defense forces which participated in the [[Final War of the Deluge]] in combat operations against [[Varshan]].

==Criteria==

Eligibility for the Service Medal is used as a criteria for eligibility for grants under the [[League of Nations Wartime Benefit Fund]].
